article.title: Ceuta crisis: ‘No evidence Morocco behind border surge’
article.summary: There is no evidence Morocco was behind the mass influx of migrants that overwhelmed the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in July, Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez told lawmakers Thursday. Sanchez's comments followed a police report that emerged this week saying that the mass entry into Ceuta was not a spontaneous migration event but a planned and phased operation designed to overwhelm border controls.

article.title: Spain's Sanchez says no 'solid proof' that Morocco planned Ceuta crisis
article.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has told lawmakers that there is no evidence the Ceuta migrant crisis was orchestrated by Morocco's government. His remarks come a day after tens of thousands of people took part in protests across the country to criticize his handling of the migrant influx. He acknowledged that Ceuta was both a humanitarian crisis and an administrative challenge. But he rejected the findings of a police report that seemed to lay blame on Morocco. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.

article.title: The Ceuta border breach was leapt on by Europe’s right. That doesn’t absolve Spain | María Ramírez
article.summary: The government’s sluggish response has been disastrous for everyone involved – and for Sánchez’s message on immigrationMore than a month after an estimated 72,000 people suddenly crossed from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta, the city remains in chaos and the damage inflicted on the Spanish government is becoming clearer. Most of those who made the crossing have returned to Morocco. The scale of the incident was nevertheless extraordinary, and about 140 peopleare thought to have died.Also extraordinary was the response of the22 EU governmentsthat rounded on the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, rather than demonstrate the solidarity one might expect from allies. Perhaps less surprising was the exploitation of the crisis by rightwing and far-right parties in Spain and beyond,Donald Trump’s attacksand the interventions ofRussian state-linked actorsandIsraeli criticson social media tofuel division.Continue reading...
